title: Writing: Traditions in My Family
writingModel: My family has always had strong Nauryz traditions. When I was a child, Nauryz was the most exciting time of the year. My mother used to start cooking two days before the holiday. She would make enormous pots of Nauryz kozhe using my great-grandmother's secret recipe.

On the morning of Nauryz, we used to clean the whole house together — even my father helped! Then we all put on our traditional clothes. My grandmother used to wear a beautiful white dress embroidered with golden patterns. She looked incredible.

The best part was the celebration outside. Our whole street used to come together. Neighbours used to bring food and share everything. There was always music — someone played the dombra, and children danced. My grandfather used to tell stories about the old days while we all sat and listened.
My favourite tradition was the swing. My uncles used to build a large Altybakan every year. We would swing for hours and sing traditional songs. I always felt incredibly happy on those days.

Today, our family still celebrates Nauryz, but some things have changed. We don't set up the outdoor swing anymore, and the celebrations are smaller. But the spirit — the feeling of community, forgiveness, and new beginnings — is still there. I hope these traditions will continue for many generations.
